clue.text: Sink the church's image

parts.note: CE is the Church of England, and the possessive adds S
spit as in 'the spit of', the spitting image of someone

explanation.surface: A remark about sinking a church's statue or reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sink' looks like a verb but is the noun: a sink of filth.
explanation.definitionFit: A sink in the sense of a pit or receptacle for waste water and filth is a synonym.

clue.text: In a pet, having nothing on show

indicators.note: the naked state is put in the middle of the pet word

parts.note: a cat is a typical pet
bare means unclothed

explanation.surface: A naked person, in a fit of temper, putting on a display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a pet' reads as the idiom for being in a temper; here the pet is the animal that is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a form of entertainment, a nightclub floor show.

clue.text: Exotics about to provide club

indicators.note: the outsiders wrap around the providing word

parts.note: exotics are foreign things or people, strangers
to afford is to provide or supply

explanation.surface: Foreigners getting ready to supply a cudgel.
explanation.walkthrough: STAFFORD RANGERS is an English non-league football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A football club, the club sense here being a sporting team rather than a weapon.

clue.text: Fish stick which is absolutely plain

parts.note: a pike is a freshwater fish
a staff is a walking stick

explanation.surface: A fishing rod described as perfectly ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition rests on the idiom 'as plain as a pikestaff', meaning perfectly obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'plain as a pikestaff' makes this the standard of complete obviousness.

clue.text: Winner audible at last?

definitions.meaning: in card games a ... card beats any card of another suit
the Last ... is the trumpet call sounding on Judgement Day, heard at the end of the world

explanation.surface: Someone who wins is finally heard.
explanation.walkthrough: Not a homophone: 'audible at last' alludes to the Last Trump of the Requiem's Tuba mirum.
explanation.definitionFit: A trump card is the winning card, and the trumpet sounding at the end of time is the Last Trump.

clue.text: Club's about turn on his awful first bloomer

indicators.note: placed on, after, the previous letters
the club letters go round the turning letter

parts.note: FC is a football club; the 's is a link
U as in a U-turn

indicators.note: awful signals the word his is mangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
A, as in A1 or grade A, means first-class

explanation.surface: A football club turns round on a terrible first blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' reads as a mistake, but it is a flowering plant. 'awful' rearranges HIS as HSI.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuchsia is a flowering shrub, so it is literally something that blooms.

clue.text: "Not many take Christmas": a report by climber

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: few means not many, nick means take, Yule is Christmas, then A as written: FEW NICK YULE A

explanation.surface: A quoted saying about Christmas reported next to a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: Said together, FEW NICK YULE A gives the sound of the answer in a non-rhotic accent.
explanation.definitionFit: A funicular is a cable railway that climbs a steep slope.

clue.text: Number on its own is just the same

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
lone means alone, on its own

explanation.surface: A number standing alone is identical.
explanation.definitionFit: A clone is an exact copy, something identical to its original.

clue.text: Protective plate for Antipodean contest?

parts.note: Sheffield plate is silver-plated copper made in that city
a shield is a protective piece of armour

explanation.surface: A protective plate is offered as an Australian prize.
explanation.walkthrough: The SHEFFIELD SHIELD is Australia's interstate first-class cricket competition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sheffield Shield is the domestic cricket championship of Australia, an antipodean contest.

clue.text: Leaders with Sun have briefly got let off

parts.note: A and B lead the alphabet
Sol is the Latin name for the sun
the contraction 've is short for have

explanation.surface: Leaders and the Sun newspaper have been excused.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to free them from blame, to pardon or excuse.

clue.text: Club sees club bank runs off bowling

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run; runs gives two
an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket

explanation.surface: One club watches another as a bank's runs come off the bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges CLUBBANK plus RR into BLACKBURN R; BLACKBURN ROVERS is a Lancashire football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A Football League club from Blackburn, Lancashire, so a club in the sporting sense.

clue.text: Overhead workers reported to Norman king

indicators.note: reported signals a word judged by its sound

parts.note: roofers work above people's heads

explanation.surface: Workers on the roof have been reported to the king.
explanation.walkthrough: William II, son of the Conqueror, was nicknamed Rufus.
explanation.definitionFit: William Rufus was the second Norman king of England.

clue.text: Fuddled Kelt with cup of rye in rhyme

indicators.note: fuddled means drunk and confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk Celt with a cup of rye whisky reciting poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'Sing a Song of Sixpence' has 'a pocket full of rye'; the 'of' joins fodder to definition in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme the rye comes as a pocketful, so this is the measure of rye in that verse.

clue.text: Pitch-black object with backing left to sin, a naughty boy

indicators.note: backing tells you the whole run of pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: to err is to sin
a brat is a badly behaved child

explanation.surface: A dark thing pushes a naughty boy towards sin.
explanation.walkthrough: A tar barrel holds pitch, so it is a pitch-black object.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrel of tar, used for bonfires, contains pitch and is black with it.

clue.text: Assistant to bow before knight's horse

parts.note: rosin is rubbed on a violin bow to help it grip the strings
ante is Latin for before

explanation.surface: A helper bowing before a knight's mount.
explanation.walkthrough: The knight is Don Quixote, whose horse is Rosinante. 'bow' is the violinist's bow, not a bending.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocinante, also spelt Rosinante, is the nag ridden by Don Quixote.

clue.text: Not all the rest, say

indicators.note: say signals the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: peace means rest or quiet

explanation.surface: A remark about the rest being only part.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a part of something, so not the whole of it.

clue.text: Receiver now at ease, they say

parts.note: present means now, the current time

indicators.note: they say signals the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the word sounds like the letter E twice

explanation.surface: Someone receiving something is now relaxed, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: A presentee is someone to whom a present is given, the person receiving.

clue.text: Flourish put on back burners?

indicators.note: putting the word on its back turns it round

parts.note: fires are burners

explanation.surface: A flourish added to the rear burners of a stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back burners' looks like the cooker phrase, but 'back' belongs to the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small decorative stroke on a letter, a typographic flourish.

clue.text: Boss that's been given rope

definitions.meaning: the captain of a ship or team is the boss
one who jumps with a rope

explanation.surface: A boss allowed enough rope to hang himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipper is a captain, and also one who skips with a skipping rope.

clue.text: Insurer's right to final yield

annotationWithheld.why: Insurer's right to final yield (9): the parse needs SURER with R + END inside, with the 'In' of 'Insurer's' as the container indicator, one printed word doing two jobs

clue.text: New after change of leaders, fleet is fast

indicators.note: the new letter is placed after the fleet word
the first two letters of the fleet word swap places

parts.note: an armada is a fleet of ships

explanation.surface: Something new follows a reshuffle at the top, and the fleet is speedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleet' and 'fast' both look like speed words; 'fleet' is ARMADA, 'fast' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Muslim month of fasting, so it is a period of fast.

clue.text: Absence of responsibility for local disturbance of 101 AD

parts.note: a local is a pub, an inn

indicators.note: disturbance stirs up the letters of the number

parts.note: C (a hundred) plus ONE
CE, Common Era, is the secular equivalent of AD

explanation.surface: A pub fight in the year 101 was nobody's fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbance of' rearranges C and ONE as OCEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocence is freedom from guilt or blame, so a lack of responsibility for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Aroused without former partner being summoned

indicators.note: without means the former partner is taken out

parts.note: excited means aroused
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Someone aroused without their ex is called up.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cited is to be summoned to appear in court.

clue.text: Park where 9 are actually in debt after being promoted

indicators.note: in a down clue, promoting moves the letters upward, so they read backwards

parts.note: 'do owe' is the emphatic form, actually owing

explanation.surface: Football fans are really in the red after promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: EWOOD Park is the ground of Blackburn Rovers, the 9-across team.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewood Park is the home stadium of the Blackburn football club named at 9.

clue.text: Bits of breakfast told by stains?

indicators.note: told signals a word spoken aloud, judged by its sound

parts.note: egg and ham are breakfast foods

explanation.surface: Food stains reveal what was on the breakfast plate.
explanation.walkthrough: Egham is a Surrey town next to Staines, so 'by stains' is a pun on Staines.
explanation.definitionFit: Egham lies beside Staines on the Thames, so it is found by Staines.

clue.text: Club getting rapid news on gold later died

parts.note: presto is the musical direction for very fast
N for new, doubled for the plural
or is gold in heraldry
then means later, afterwards

explanation.surface: A club receives fast news about gold, then someone dies.
explanation.walkthrough: PRESTON NORTH END is a Lancashire football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A Football League club from Preston, Lancashire, a club in the sporting sense.

clue.text: Writer in a hurry to do so, too

parts.note: rush means hurry
'do so' refers back to the previous clue, which ends 'died'

explanation.surface: An author in a hurry to follow suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do so' points to 22-across's last word, 'died'.
explanation.definitionFit: Salman Rushdie is a British-Indian novelist, a well-known writer.

clue.text: China reddens unexpectedly

indicators.note: unexpectedly signals the letters turn up in a surprising order

explanation.surface: Chinese porcelain blushes without warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is porcelain, not the country: Dresden is fine porcelain from Saxony.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresden china is porcelain made near Dresden at Meissen, a type of china.
